8	  core_claim: >
9	    Structural consistency signals are the strongest unsupervised quality estimators for LLM-based IE —
10	    entity voting leads ρ (0.38) while EM leads AUROC (0.75), with soft Jaccard as complementary robust signal
11	    (temperature-stable: NER Δρ=0.028; conditional filtering ρ=0.31). A correlation-selection gap means
12	    this does not translate to best-of-N selection — no signal reliably surpasses greedy on either task
13	    (p>0.39, bootstrap). Signal effectiveness is task-difficulty-dependent: easy tasks favor exact-match,
14	    hard tasks favor structural consistency, and SJ strength scales with both sample size (N=8→16 ρ +0.052)
15	    and instance complexity (entity count 6+ ρ=0.55). RE reveals a capability boundary: when compound
16	    error propagation dominates (~44% zero-F1), all signals weaken (ρ=0.134-0.350) — conditional filtering restores
17	    structural signal advantage (SJ ρ=0.31) while logprob collapses (ρ=-0.03).

126	    core_bullets:
127	      - "Hook: Self-consistency voting has shown remarkable gains for reasoning tasks (+18pp on GSM8K). But structured prediction (IE) has internal dependencies that surface metrics cannot capture — does consistency still help?"
128	      - "Gap: Prior work conflates quality estimation (predicting which outputs are reliable) with sample selection (choosing the best output). These are fundamentally different tasks requiring different signal properties."
129	      - "Insight: Consistency signals are instance-level aggregates that predict input difficulty, NOT sample-level discriminators that identify the best output. This explains why high correlation (ρ up to 0.50) fails to enable selection."
130	      - "Contributions: (C1) First systematic comparison of 5 confidence signals for quality estimation in generative IE; (C2) Identification of the correlation-selection gap; (C3) Task-complexity boundary — signal ranking depends on task difficulty"
131	      - "Contextualize negative result: non-obvious because self-consistency works for reasoning, and structural prediction has richer internal structure"

143	    core_bullets:
144	      - "Opening: Position in landscape via surveys — Confidence Estimation Survey (Geng et al., NAACL 2024, arXiv 2311.08298) + Abstention Survey (Feng et al., TACL 2025) + UQ Survey (ACL Findings 2025) + UQ&CC Survey (arXiv 2503.15850). Our work bridges confidence estimation and selective prediction for structured outputs."
145	      - "Cluster 1 — Self-consistency & LLM agreement: Wang 2023 (SC-CoT), USC Chen 2024, SelfCheckGPT Manakul 2023, Atomic SC (EMNLP 2024, sub-claim consistency for long-form text). Differentiation: all use exact-match or text-level comparison on discrete/text outputs; we use set-theoretic structural similarity on entity/relation sets."
146	      - "NEW Cluster — Test-Time Scaling & Sample Selection (dedicated subsection): CISC (ACL Findings 2025, arXiv 2502.06233, confidence-weighted majority vote), Self-Certainty BoN (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2502.18581, KL-divergence selection), ReASC (arXiv 2601.02970, adaptive sampling), Ranked Voting SC (arXiv 2505.10772), Latent SC (arXiv 2508.18395). KEY FRAMING: ALL operate on reasoning/QA with discrete answer spaces. We are FIRST to (a) extend SC to set-valued structured outputs (IE), (b) discover correlation-selection gap: strong quality estimation ↛ selection ability. Self-Certainty BoN is direct academic dialogue: they demonstrate reward-free selection works for reasoning; we show it FAILS for structured IE NER."
147	      - "NEW Cluster — Consistency for Structured IE (dedicated subsection): Nédellec & Xia (Genomics Informatics, 2026-02, PMC12888769) — most direct competitor: consistency-accuracy correlation in hard-prompted LLMs for NER/RE on plant-health data. KEY DIFFERENTIATION: (a) they use surface-level string matching, self-acknowledge limitation ('overlooks semantically consistent outputs') — our SJ directly addresses this; (b) no best-of-N selection study; (c) single-domain hard-prompted (T=0); (d) no multi-signal family comparison. CoCoA (Vashurin et al., NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2502.04964) — MBR framework fusing confidence+consistency for UQ on QA/summarization/translation, parallels our exp-016 ensemble but not structured IE. Vashurin et al. (arXiv 2510.20460, 2025) — systematic evaluation of 4 UQ methods (VCE/MSP/SC/CoCoA), tasks exclude structured IE. FRAMING: Nédellec & Xia's surface-matching limitation motivates SJ; CoCoA's confidence+consistency fusion parallels our ensemble analysis; both confirm structured IE as underexplored."
148	      - "Cluster 2 — Uncertainty estimation & calibration: Kuhn 2023 semantic uncertainty, Semantic Entropy Probes (arXiv 2406.15927), Kadavath 2022 P(True), Guo 2017, Desai & Durrett 2020 → we compare model confidence with output-space consistency"
149	      - "Cluster 3 — Conformal prediction: Fisch 2021, Angelopoulos 2021 → guarantees coverage, not ranking"
150	      - "Cluster 4 — Token/span-level uncertainty for NER: Xiao & Wang 2019, Shelmanov 2021, He 2020 → CRF/classifier uncertainty, we study generative LLM setting"
151	      - "Cluster 5 — Ensemble & MC-dropout: Lakshminarayanan 2017, Gal & Ghahramani 2016 → require model modification; our signals are post-hoc"
152	      - "Cluster 6 — Verifier/reward models: Cobbe 2021, Lightman 2023 → supervised; we study unsupervised signals"
153	      - "Cluster 7 — TTS scaling theory: Snell 2024, Brown 2024 → we provide empirical evidence for IE"
154	      - "Cluster 8 — IE confidence & selective prediction: Culotta & McCallum 2004, Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017, Jagannatha & Yu 2022 → pre-LLM approaches"

218	    core_bullets:
219	      - "Problem formulation: given LLM M, input x, N stochastic samples {y_1,...,y_N}, define confidence signal c(x, {y_i}) → ℝ"
220	      - "Signal 1 — Log-probability: c_lp(y_i) = (1/|y_i|) Σ log p(t_j|t_{<j}, x). Per-sample signal. Clarify: sequence-level mean, not token-level max."
221	      - "Signal 2 — Exact-match voting: c_em(x) = max_y |{i: y_i = y}| / N. Instance-level."
222	      - "Signal 3 — Fleiss' Kappa (FK): token-level inter-rater agreement. Instance-level."
223	      - "Signal 4 — Soft Jaccard (SJ): set-aware structural similarity via type-grouped bipartite matching. Instance-level. Key: uses Hungarian matching with max(|A|,|B|) normalization."
224	      - "Signal 5 — Entity voting confidence: per-entity majority voting rate, averaged. Instance-level."
225	      - "Distinction: log-prob is PER-SAMPLE (ranks candidates), others are INSTANCE-LEVEL (aggregate across samples). This distinction is central to the correlation-selection gap."
226	      - "Evaluation: quality estimation (ρ, τ, AUROC vs F1) and sample selection (best-of-N F1)"

meta:
  venue: EMNLP 2026 Main (via ARR May)
  track: main
  template: null  # ARR/ACL format — need to download acl2023.sty or latest ARR template
  template_note: "No local template found. Worker should download latest ARR LaTeX template from ACL Rolling Review."
  page_limit: 8  # + unlimited references
  deadline: 2026-05-25
  core_claim: >
    Structural consistency signals are the strongest unsupervised quality estimators for LLM-based IE —
    entity voting leads ρ (0.38) while EM leads AUROC (0.75), with soft Jaccard as complementary robust signal
    (temperature-stable: NER Δρ=0.028; conditional filtering ρ=0.31). A correlation-selection gap means
    this does not translate to best-of-N selection — no signal reliably surpasses greedy on either task
    (p>0.39, bootstrap). Signal effectiveness is task-difficulty-dependent: easy tasks favor exact-match,
    hard tasks favor structural consistency, and SJ strength scales with both sample size (N=8→16 ρ +0.052)
    and instance complexity (entity count 6+ ρ=0.55). RE reveals a capability boundary: when compound
    error propagation dominates (~44% zero-F1), all signals weaken (ρ=0.134-0.350) — conditional filtering restores
    structural signal advantage (SJ ρ=0.31) while logprob collapses (ρ=-0.03).
  created_at: 2026-05-14T13:00:00Z
  selected_title: "Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: A Systematic Comparison of Confidence Signals for Test-Time Scaling in Information Extraction"
  director_approval: "2026-05-14 approved with modifications: title #2 selected, RE must distinguish joint vs RE-only protocol (D023), 3 tables confirmed (tab_robustness kept), exp_003/exp_007 pending — Director will notify for Patch"
  re_protocol_note: "D023: Joint RE SJ ρ=0.267 < FK ρ=0.315; RE-only SJ ρ=0.304 > FK ρ=0.269. Table 1 must label protocol. Discussion must address joint error propagation."
  d024_re_data_update: >
    D024 (2026-05-14): 3-seed N=16 T=1.0 confirms RE full set SJ NOT superior to FK.
    FORBIDDEN: claim "SJ consistently outperforms FK across all tasks".
    Correct narrative: NER SJ robust > FK; RE full set all signals weak + indistinguishable (~44% zero-F1);
    RE conditional set SJ recovers advantage (Δ=0.15-0.21 over FK) and logprob near-zero.
    Table 1 must include both full and conditional RE rows.
    Conditional analysis = unique contribution, emphasize in Discussion.
  d035_narrative_update: >
    D035 (2026-05-14): Heatmap data source unified to exp_015. NER full: voting ρ=0.502 (was 0.392),
    SJ ρ=0.357 (was 0.383). Voting significantly leads SJ (NER +0.145), NOT "statistically equivalent".
    FORBIDDEN: "SJ ≈ voting". Correct: same family, complementary — voting strongest per-instance,
    SJ more robust cross-condition. SJ unique value: (a) temperature numerically stable (RE Δρ=0.010, NER Δρ=0.014; bootstrap CI includes 0, not statistically significant),
    (b) generalizes to any structured output not limited to entity, (c) conditional filtering ρ=0.412,
    (d) ensemble with voting AUROC 0.735 complementary.
    exp_009 findings (Claim 3): SJ high entity count (6+) ρ=0.547, low (1-2) ρ=0.415;
    SJ >> logprob advantage stable across all sentence length quartiles (Δρ≈0.08-0.20);
    two proxies (entity count, sentence length) weakly correlated with F1 (|r|<0.15, measuring input complexity not output quality) but moderately correlated with each other (ρ=0.650, overlapping dimensions). CORRECTED 2026-05-14: was "three independent proxies" — proxy-proxy correlation is NOT weak; only proxy-F1 correlation is weak.
  d037_n16_re_refinement: >
    D037 (2026-05-14): N=16 NER (exp_001_seed42_v2/seed123_v2): SJ ρ=0.428/0.424, cross-seed Δ<0.01.
    N=8→16 SJ +0.071, FK +0.016 — SJ scaling gain >> FK. RE N=16 (exp_008_re_n16_v2):
    full logprob ρ=0.287 > SJ 0.281 ≈ FK 0.279 (all ~flat, compound error ceiling).
    RE cond: SJ ρ=0.308 vs logprob ρ=-0.026 (p=0.685, logprob completely fails).
    FORBIDDEN: "structural signals universally outperform logprob" — only true within model capability range.
    Unified framework: structural signals strongest within model capability range; beyond it, all signals converge.
    RE 44% zero-F1 must be noted as limitation in paper.
  d038_temperature_precision: >
    D038 (2026-05-14): Temperature robustness must distinguish NER vs RE.
    SJ NER Δρ=0.014 (MODERATE), SJ RE Δρ=0.010 (ROBUST). FORBIDDEN: generic "SJ Δρ≤0.01".
    FK NER Δρ=0.06, RE Δρ=0.097 — FK temperature sensitivity confirmed.
    Bootstrap 95% CI all include 0 → NOT statistically significant.
    FORBIDDEN: "significantly" for temperature differences → use "numerically small".
    "Conditional filtering >> temperature tuning" scope excludes logprob (no T=0.7 logprob data),
    paper must note this limitation.
  d049_n8_vs_n16_labeling: >
    D049 (2026-05-14): SciERC uses N=16, CoNLL uses N=8. Tables MUST annotate N per row.
    Limitations must discuss N's impact on consistency estimation stability.
    No N=16 CoNLL experiment (cost unjustified). Table format: include N column or footnote.
  d050_conll_headroom_honesty: >

  - section: method
    word_budget: 1000
    core_bullets:
      - "Problem formulation: given LLM M, input x, N stochastic samples {y_1,...,y_N}, define confidence signal c(x, {y_i}) → ℝ"
      - "Signal 1 — Log-probability: c_lp(y_i) = (1/|y_i|) Σ log p(t_j|t_{<j}, x). Per-sample signal. Clarify: sequence-level mean, not token-level max."
      - "Signal 2 — Exact-match voting: c_em(x) = max_y |{i: y_i = y}| / N. Instance-level."
      - "Signal 3 — Fleiss' Kappa (FK): token-level inter-rater agreement. Instance-level."
      - "Signal 4 — Soft Jaccard (SJ): set-aware structural similarity via type-grouped bipartite matching. Instance-level. Key: uses Hungarian matching with max(|A|,|B|) normalization."
      - "Signal 5 — Entity voting confidence: per-entity majority voting rate, averaged. Instance-level."
      - "Distinction: log-prob is PER-SAMPLE (ranks candidates), others are INSTANCE-LEVEL (aggregate across samples). This distinction is central to the correlation-selection gap."
      - "Evaluation: quality estimation (ρ, τ, AUROC vs F1) and sample selection (best-of-N F1)"

DGS is ablation evidence, not core contribution.\\n\\n## Story Spine (D157 — Triple Contribution: QE + Diagnostic + Prescriptive, Main Conference)\\n\\n**Problem**: Test-time scaling via multi-sample generation improves LLM reasoning, but its effectiveness for structured information extraction is unclear. Practitioners need to know: (1) can confidence signals estimate output quality? (2) can they select better outputs? (3) if not, what SHOULD they do instead?\\n\\n**Existing approaches & gaps**: Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) succeeds for discrete-answer reasoning via majority vote on discrete answers. MBR decoding succeeds for MT. But structured IE outputs (entity sets, relation triples) present a fundamentally different challenge — prior work applies instance-level selection (pick one of N complete outputs), which is the wrong analogy for set-structured outputs. We show the correct analogy is entity-level construction (aggregate across outputs).\\n\\n**Our framing (D157 — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION)**:\\n\\n**Contribution A (Positive — QE Framework)**: Five confidence signals across four families reliably predict structured IE output quality (AUROC 0.82, ρ 0.45). Signal ranking is task-dependent: structural > probabilistic for NER, reversed for RE. QE enables selective prediction: filtering 20% low-confidence instances yields +5-8pp F1 gain (AUPRC 0.70-0.92, VC strongest signal).\\n\\n**Contribution B (Diagnostic — Why Instance-Level Selection Fails)**:\\n1. **Design property**: 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction.\\n2. **Instance Degeneracy**: 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom.\\n3. **LP Compression**: Logprob within-instance range compressed (0.041 nats). Free-form ablation confirms intrinsic (std ratio 0.97).\\n4. **Multi-causal**: LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy 3× (7.2% vs 21%) and increases oracle headroom (+2.7pp), but ALL selection methods still fail to beat greedy → low degeneracy is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT.\\n5. **Capability-diversity tension**: Higher capability → more convergence → more degeneracy. CoNLL 91% F1→58% degen, SciERC 66%→21%.\\n6. **LP alignment as primary predictor**: LP selection viability depends on within-instance ρ(LP,F1). Few-NERD (ρ~0.5-0.7) → LP +1.38pp (p<0.05). SciERC (ρ~0.2) → LP fails despite similar degeneracy. Cross-dataset degeneracy ρ=0.052 (23 configs, p=0.81).\\n\\n**Contribution C (Prescriptive — Entity-Level Construction + Practitioner Protocol, D157)**:\\nThe correct self-consistency analogy for structured IE is NOT instance-level selection but entity-level construction: aggregate entities across N samples via majority vote, constructing a new output from parts.\\n- **Entity construction (multi-seed N=8 mean)**: SciERC +1.02pp, FewNERD +1.40pp, CoNLL +0.10pp (n.s.). Mechanism: recall gain by aggregating low-frequency correct entities across samples.\\n- **72B zero-shot construction**: LP-weighted construction SciERC ZS +1.53pp (stronger than fine-tuned!), CoNLL ZS -0.37pp (headroom-limited). **θ=2/N fails in zero-shot** (SciERC -0.52pp, CoNLL -0.92pp) → LP-weighting is necessary in zero-shot regime.\\n- **Construction effectiveness is headroom-dependent**: Works when oracle headroom is sufficient (SciERC 15pp → +1.53pp), fails when near ceiling (CoNLL 5.3pp → -0.37pp). Signals are ALWAYS useful for flagging uncertain instances, even when they cannot improve selection.\\n\\n**Headline**: \\\"We present a triple contribution for structured IE test-time scaling: (1) a QE framework showing confidence signals reliably predict output quality and enable selective prediction (+5-8pp @80% coverage); (2) a diagnostic revealing that the correlation-selection gap is fundamental — persisting from 4B to 72B and from fine-tuned to zero-shot regimes — driven by degeneracy, LP compression, and LP-alignment misalignment; and (3) entity-level construction as a diagnostic-motivated mitigation that significantly improves over greedy decoding (+1.02pp SciERC, +1.40pp FewNERD fine-tuned; +1.53pp SciERC zero-shot via LP-weighting), with effectiveness governed by oracle headroom.\\\"\\n\\n**Title candidates**:\\n- \\\"Don't Select, Construct: Diagnosing and Fixing Test-Time Scaling for Structured Information Extraction\\\"\\n- \\\"Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: From Diagnosis to Entity-Level Construction for Structured IE\\\"\\n- \\\"Beyond Selection: Entity-Level Construction as the Correct Self-Consistency for Structured IE\\\"\\n\\n## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns\\n\\n### R1: \\\"Only one NER dataset — generalization unclear\\\"\\n- **Status**: ✅ RESOLVED. 3 NER datasets (SciERC + CoNLL-2003 + Few-NERD INTRA) × 2 models (Qwen3-8B + LLaMA-3.1-8B) + scale ablation (Qwen3-4B). Entity construction θ=2/N (+1.02pp SciERC, +1.40pp FewNERD, multi-seed N=8 mean). **72B zero-shot confirms gap is fundamental**: LP ρ=-0.002 (CoNLL) / 0.081 (SciERC); LP-weighted construction +1.53pp (SciERC ZS); θ=2/N fails in zero-shot (-0.52pp SciERC, -0.92pp CoNLL). ## Target Venue
- Primary: EMNLP 2026 **Main Conference** (via ARR May 2026)
- Deadline: ARR May cycle, 2026-05-25

## Core Claims (D157 updated — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION: QE + diagnostic + prescriptive)

### Claim 1 (PRIMARY — Dual Contribution: QE Framework + Selection Diagnostic)
**Positive contribution (A)**: Confidence signals reliably predict structured IE output quality at the population level (AUROC up to 0.82, ρ up to 0.45), enabling practical QE/selective prediction.
**Diagnostic contribution (B)** (D154 revised): Selection viability depends on LP signal quality and dataset characteristics, not degeneracy alone:
- **Degeneracy as headroom predictor**: High degeneracy eliminates selection headroom (CoNLL 47.4% degen → 0 net gain). Within fixed dataset-model settings, degeneracy causally modulates LP effectiveness (SciERC epoch ablation: −1.18/+0.74/+0.99pp at 3/5/10 epochs; per-entity-type within Few-NERD ρ=−0.881). But across datasets, degeneracy alone does NOT predict LP selection direction (23-point cross-configuration ρ=0.052, p=0.81).
- **LP-quality alignment as primary predictor**: LP must track entity-level F1 within instances. Few-NERD within-instance ρ(LP,F1) ≈ 0.5-0.66 → LP selection +1.36pp (p<0.05). SciERC ρ(LP,F1) ≈ 0.18-0.24 → LP fails despite similar degeneracy (17.8% vs 13.8%). This is the primary determinant of LP selection success across datasets.
- **Structural signals (SJ/FK/EM/VC)**: universally fail regardless — instance-level aggregates cannot rank candidates by construction.
- **Multi-causal diagnosis (D154)**: (1) degeneracy modulates headroom within settings; (2) LP-quality alignment determines cross-dataset selection success; (3) LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy (7.2% vs 17.8%) AND improves LP spread (0.057 vs 0.041 nats) but SciERC's weak LP-F1 alignment (ρ~0.24) still prevents selection success → LP alignment is the binding constraint, degeneracy is a within-setting modulator.

The framing is NOT "selection fails" (pure negative) but "we characterize WHEN LP works (strong LP-F1 alignment), WHY it fails elsewhere (weak alignment + compression), and WHAT distinguishes LP from structural signals" (empirical characterization with diagnostic implications).

**Three-layer argument + Capability-diversity tension**:
- Layer A (design property, noted not discovered): 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction. This is a conceptual clarification — the "methodological premise" — not an empirical finding.
- Layer B (empirical — instance degeneracy): 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom. Within-instance ρ=0.524 (SciERC) and 0.994 (CoNLL) — signals ARE correlated within instances, but degeneracy makes this irrelevant. Non-degenerate instances show MBR closing 23-41% of oracle gap. Selection recovers T=1.0 sampling degradation (LP 0.647 vs Random 0.610, +3.7pp) but only matches T=0 greedy (0.645 macro) at 8× inference cost — zero marginal gain.
- Layer C (empirical — LP-quality alignment, revised D123): LP selection requires adequate within-instance correlation with task quality. Few-NERD ρ(LP,F1)≈0.5-0.66 → selection succeeds (+1.36pp). SciERC ρ(LP,F1)≈0.18-0.24 → selection fails even when LP range is adequate (rank=8: 0.057 nats). LP compression (median range 0.041 nats on SciERC full-rank) is a contributing factor but NOT the sole explanation — rank=8 expands LP range to 0.057 yet still fails. Entity-token LP shows 4× variance but WORSE selection (-2.0pp). Free-form ablation confirms compression is model/task intrinsic for NER (std ratio 0.97).
- **Capability-diversity tension** (unifying insight, D111): Model capability → output convergence → instance degeneracy → vanishing selection headroom. Evidence: CoNLL (91% F1) → 58% degeneracy, SciERC (66% F1) → 21%, WNUT (48% F1) → ~0%. Scale dimension: 8B → 21% degen vs 4B → 10.4% on SciERC. This is NOT an "artifact" — it is a **consequence of capability**, a structural inevitability. The better the model, the less test-time scaling can help via unsupervised selection.

**Distinction from MBR literature**: Eikema et al.'s MBR failure = utility function misalignment. Our failure = utility IS aligned (within-instance ρ=0.524) but headroom eliminated by degeneracy — qualitatively novel mechanism.

**Key evidence (score compression)**:
- Non-tied subset (40%): logprob selection +2.9pp vs greedy (p=0.01), within-instance ρ: 0.08→0.39
- Full set: logprob +0.6pp, bootstrap p=0.39, Cohen's d=0.038 (negligible), 95% CI [-3.0, +4.2]pp
- Oracle headroom: NER +13pp, RE +18pp → information exists but signals can't access it

**Key evidence (free-form ablation)** [DONE — exp_freeform_ablation, NEGATIVE]:
- LP distribution: constrained std=0.0206, free-form std=0.0199 (ratio 0.97, virtually unchanged)
- Tied fraction: 59.7% → 57.7% (-2.0pp, negligible)
- NER selection: +0.59pp → +0.18pp (both negligible vs greedy)
- RE selection: -0.68pp → +1.69pp (flipped positive — secondary finding)
- NER VC rho: 0.379 → 0.409 (slight QE improvement, selection still fails)
- Parse rate: 99.95% (fine-tuned model retains JSON format without grammar)
- **Conclusion**: Score compression is model/task intrinsic. The gap is universal.

**Key evidence (scale ablation)** [DONE — 2×2 matrix: {CoNLL, SciERC} × {Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-4B}]:
- CoNLL NER: 4B greedy_f1=0.9234 (>8B 0.9123, +1.11pp), SJ_ρ=0.4217 (≈8B 0.4357, −1.4pp), FK_ρ=0.4181 (>8B 0.3998, +1.83pp)

- SciERC RE: 4B SJ_ρ=0.2673 (>8B 0.2441, +2.32pp), FK_ρ=0.3593 (>8B 0.2782, +8.11pp); struct>surface ✗ at both scales
- **Conclusion**: Correlation strength maintained or improved at 4B across all 4 cells. The gap originates from within-instance signal misalignment, not model capacity. Task difficulty (SciERC RE zero-F1 rate) remains the primary driver, consistent across scales.
- CoNLL 4B headroom: 1.70pp (vs 8B 4.20pp) → MARGINAL for selection power, but QE correlations robust
- SciERC RE 4B: 47.6% zero-F1, RE LP_ρ_cond=0.1135 (p=0.074, n.s.) → confirms binary dominance at 4B
- **4B selection results** (correlation-selection gap at 4B):
  - CoNLL NER 4B (n=2756): SJ +0.07pp, FK +0.03pp, LP +0.09pp vs greedy 0.9213. All ≤0.1pp — MARGINAL (headroom 1.70pp)
  - SciERC NER 4B (n=529): SJ **-1.49pp**, FK -1.56pp, LP -2.23pp vs greedy 0.6622. Oracle 0.7925 (+13.02pp). **All signals WORSE than greedy despite 13pp oracle headroom — gap confirmed at 4B**
  - SciERC NER 4B gap demonstration: SJ-FK ρ gap = +0.096 (strong correlation advantage), SJ-FK selection F1 gap = +0.0007 (zero selection advantage) → correlation-selection gap quantified at 4B

- Dataset: Few-NERD INTRA coarse 8-type, 131k train, 32,565 test (gold-filtered)
- Degeneracy: 10.0% (vs SciERC 21%, CoNLL 58%) — lowest in our study

- **Key insight**: LP succeeds where LP-F1 alignment is strong; structural signals fail regardless. But cross-dataset, the gradient CoNLL→SciERC→Few-NERD does NOT monotonically predict LP effectiveness (D154: ρ=0.052 at 23 points).

**Bonus finding (parse rate)**: Free-form parse rate 99.95% (4406/4408) — fine-tuned 8B model generates valid JSON without grammar constraints. Challenges intro:19 claim about constrained decoding necessity for format compliance.

**Implications**: Not just "signals don't work" but "here's WHY they don't work (intrinsic score compression), here's proof it's universal (controlled ablation via elimination), and here's the forward direction (breaking LP compression requires fundamentally different approaches — trained verifiers, multi-round refinement — not simply relaxing decoding constraints)."

### Claim 2 (METHODOLOGY — QE Evaluation Framework)
Systematic evaluation of 5 confidence signals across 4 families for structured IE quality estimation. This is the methodological infrastructure, not a primary contribution.

**Key results**:
- NER: EM AUROC 0.749, voting_conf ρ=0.379, SJ ρ=0.360 — all >> logprob (AUROC 0.578, ρ=0.205). 3-seed consistent: SJ > FK delta=0.093~0.122
- RE (3-seed confirmed): **LP > SJ > FK** (mean ρ: LP 0.302, SJ 0.265, FK 0.254). Signal ranking reverses vs NER — structural signals lose advantage when 43-45% of RE samples have F1=0 (binary signal dominance). LP's coarse but stable generation-confidence signal captures "did the model get any relations right" better than structural overlap measures.

T=0.7: LP full ρ improves 0.205→0.249, LP cond ρ 0.154→0.185; FK 0.267→0.289 despite more compression → concentrated signal hypothesis (non-tied instances at lower T carry more informative variance). **Paper citation rule**: robustness/temperature tables use full ρ; score compression analysis uses cond ρ. Always annotate which variant.
- **Task-dependent signal effectiveness** (new finding from RE 3-seed): The optimal signal family depends on task structure. NER (token-level, graded F1) → structural agreement captures quality gradients. RE (relation-level, binary-dominated F1) → logprob captures generation confidence better. This is NOT a weakness — it's a nuanced finding that enriches the diagnostic framework.

- NER full (n=529): ρ — voting_conf 0.379, SJ 0.360, EM 0.295, FK 0.267, logprob 0.205; AUROC — EM 0.749, SJ 0.692, voting_conf 0.684, FK 0.629, logprob 0.578

**4B selection evidence** (N=8, T=1.0):
- CoNLL NER 4B (n=2756): greedy 0.9213, SJ 0.9220 (+0.07pp), FK 0.9215, LP 0.9221 (+0.09pp), oracle 0.9382. Headroom 1.70pp → selection indistinguishable
- SciERC NER 4B (n=529): greedy 0.6622, SJ 0.6473 (-1.49pp), FK 0.6466 (-1.56pp), LP 0.6399 (-2.23pp), oracle 0.7925 (+13.02pp). **All signals worse than greedy** → correlation-selection gap at 4B confirmed

**exp_016_rerun_1024_bootstrap evidence** (3-seed bootstrap, 1000 iterations):
- NER logprob vs greedy: bootstrap 95% CI [−0.030, +0.042], permutation p=0.39
- Effect size: Cohen's d=0.038 (negligible), sign test win rate=0.466

### Claim 3 (Diagnostic — task-complexity boundary + task-dependent signal effectiveness)
The effectiveness of consistency-based confidence is governed by task structural complexity: compound error propagation in relational tasks degrades the consistency-accuracy correlation on the full instance set, but the signal remains valid within the model's capability range. This boundary applies across all confidence signals tested.

**RE 3-seed mechanism** (D073, confirmed at 4B): 43-47% of RE samples have F1=0 (8B: 43-45%, 4B: 47.6%), creating binary-dominated signal distributions where structural overlap (SJ/FK) cannot differentiate quality gradients. Pattern consistent across model scales — confirming task difficulty, not model capacity, drives this boundary. LP's generation confidence captures "complete failure vs partial success" more reliably. 3-seed RE QE: LP ρ=0.302 > SJ 0.265 > FK 0.254. **Definitive binary dominance evidence**: RE LP full ρ=0.266 but cond ρ=0.011 (p=0.86, completely n.s.) — LP's entire RE signal comes from the zero/nonzero F1 split; once conditioned on samples where the model extracts at least one relation, LP has zero predictive power for RE quality gradients. In contrast, NER LP cond ρ remains informative (0.154–0.185). This provides the concrete mechanism for Claim 3's task-complexity boundary: it's not just "compound error" in the abstract — it's specifically the high zero-F1 rate that shifts the optimal signal family from structural to probabilistic, and LP's RE advantage is entirely a binary classification effect, not genuine quality estimation.

**MVP evidence**: RE full vs cond AUROC lift — EM: 0.706→0.752 (+4.6pp), SJ: 0.670→0.646 (−2.4pp, 待确认), voting_conf: 0.694→0.642 (−5.2pp, 待确认). Component decomposition shows all RE components equally weak (head_sj rho=0.210). T=0.7 naturally separates knowledge-gap vs uncertainty errors.

**exp-005 evidence**: Conditional filtering dwarfs temperature tuning — RE SJ cond lift +0.07~0.14 vs temperature effect ±0.01. T=1.0 preserves more oracle headroom (RE: 0.167 vs 0.131) and diversity (1-SJ: 0.389 vs 0.313). Recommendation: T=1.0 + conditional filtering, not temperature optimization.

**exp-001 N-scaling evidence** (SciERC, n=200 subset, ⚠️ needs full-set confirmation):
- RE N=16: voting_conf ρ=0.448 (vs N=8 0.340, +0.108), SJ ρ=0.333 (vs 0.244, +0.089), all signals improve +0.07~0.10
- NER N=16: flat (already saturated at N=8) — voting_conf 0.401 vs 0.392
- **Key insight**: The task-complexity boundary is partially a SAMPLE BUDGET boundary. Compound error propagation increases per-instance variance, requiring more samples (N=16 vs N=8) to average out noise. This makes Claim 2 more nuanced: RE consistency fails at N=8 not because the signal is absent, but because it's noisier and needs more samples to manifest.
- ⚠️ Caveat: exp-001 ran on 200/529 instances. Full-set replication needed before claiming in paper.

### Claim 4 (D154: Empirical Characterization of Selection Boundaries)
**Contribution C (Selection Boundary Characterization)**: Empirical analysis of when and why LP selection succeeds or fails, with DGS as exploratory heuristic (not validated framework).
- **Core finding (D154)**: Selection viability depends on LP signal quality (within-instance ρ(LP,F1)) and dataset characteristics. Cross-dataset degeneracy-LP correlation is ρ=0.052 (23 points, p=0.81) — degeneracy alone does not predict selection direction. Within fixed settings, degeneracy causally modulates LP effectiveness (epoch ablation, temperature ablation, per-entity-type analysis).
- **DGS as explored heuristic** (demoted from "validated framework"): Mixed results across dataset×model:
  - Few-NERD Qwen: +0.92pp (significant) — strong LP alignment (ρ~0.5)
  - SciERC Qwen: +0.71pp (not significant) — weak alignment (ρ~0.2)
  - CoNLL Qwen: -0.81pp (significant negative) — high degen + weak alignment
  - CoNLL LLaMA: +0.14pp (significant positive) — LP-quality alignment adequate
  - Cross-model sign reversal on CoNLL illustrates LP alignment's role, but DGS does not constitute a reliable prescriptive method
- **MBR**: Uniformly negative, excluded. Exception: SciERC T=1.2 +1.8pp under high-diversity conditions.
- **Status**: D154 reframing complete. DGS is ablation evidence, not core contribution.

## Story Spine (D157 — Triple Contribution: QE + Diagnostic + Prescriptive, Main Conference)

**Problem**: Test-time scaling via multi-sample generation improves LLM reasoning, but its effectiveness for structured information extraction is unclear. Practitioners need to know: (1) can confidence signals estimate output quality? (2) can they select better outputs? (3) if not, what SHOULD they do instead?

**Existing approaches & gaps**: Self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) succeeds for discrete-answer reasoning via majority vote on discrete answers. MBR decoding succeeds for MT. But structured IE outputs (entity sets, relation triples) present a fundamentally different challenge — prior work applies instance-level selection (pick one of N complete outputs), which is the wrong analogy for set-structured outputs. We show the correct analogy is entity-level construction (aggregate across outputs).

**Our framing (D157 — TRIPLE CONTRIBUTION)**:

**Contribution A (Positive — QE Framework)**: Five confidence signals across four families reliably predict structured IE output quality (AUROC 0.82, ρ 0.45). Signal ranking is task-dependent: structural > probabilistic for NER, reversed for RE. QE enables selective prediction: filtering 20% low-confidence instances yields +5-8pp F1 gain (AUPRC 0.70-0.92, VC strongest signal).

**Contribution B (Diagnostic — Why Instance-Level Selection Fails)**:
1. **Design property**: 4/5 signals are instance-level aggregates → cannot rank candidates by construction.
2. **Instance Degeneracy**: 21-58% of instances produce identical F1 across all N samples, eliminating selection headroom.
3. **LP Compression**: Logprob within-instance range compressed (0.041 nats). Free-form ablation confirms intrinsic (std ratio 0.97).
4. **Multi-causal**: LoRA rank=8 reduces degeneracy 3× (7.2% vs 21%) and increases oracle headroom (+2.7pp), but ALL selection methods still fail to beat greedy → low degeneracy is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT.
5. **Capability-diversity tension**: Higher capability → more convergence → more degeneracy. CoNLL 91% F1→58% degen, SciERC 66%→21%.
6. **LP alignment as primary predictor**: LP selection viability depends on within-instance ρ(LP,F1). Few-NERD (ρ~0.5-0.7) → LP +1.38pp (p<0.05). SciERC (ρ~0.2) → LP fails despite similar degeneracy. Cross-dataset degeneracy ρ=0.052 (23 configs, p=0.81).

**Contribution C (Prescriptive — Entity-Level Construction + Practitioner Protocol, D157)**:
The correct self-consistency analogy for structured IE is NOT instance-level selection but entity-level construction: aggregate entities across N samples via majority vote, constructing a new output from parts.
- **Entity construction (multi-seed N=8 mean)**: SciERC +1.02pp, FewNERD +1.40pp, CoNLL +0.10pp (n.s.). Mechanism: recall gain by aggregating low-frequency correct entities across samples.
- **72B zero-shot construction**: LP-weighted construction SciERC ZS +1.53pp (stronger than fine-tuned!), CoNLL ZS -0.37pp (headroom-limited). **θ=2/N fails in zero-shot** (SciERC -0.52pp, CoNLL -0.92pp) → LP-weighting is necessary in zero-shot regime.
- **Construction effectiveness is headroom-dependent**: Works when oracle headroom is sufficient (SciERC 15pp → +1.53pp), fails when near ceiling (CoNLL 5.3pp → -0.37pp). This is consistent across fine-tuned and zero-shot regimes.
- **LP-alignment gating (preliminary diagnostic)**: Probe 50 instances on validation set to compute adjusted alignment score → automatically select construction vs LP selection. 3/3 datasets correct gating. Bootstrap CI: τ=0.3 at center of [0.25, 0.35] stable plateau, routing decisions stable across τ∈[0.2, 0.4] (stability ≥95%).
- **Selective prediction**: QE-driven human-in-the-loop — retain 80% high-confidence instances, F1 +5-8pp. VC is strongest signal across all datasets.

**QE-vs-Selection Decoupling** (Dream-identified most novel insight): QE correlation (SJ ρ) is stable across LoRA rank configurations (0.360→0.378) while selection gap changes dramatically. Signals are ALWAYS useful for flagging uncertain instances, even when they cannot improve selection.

**Headline**: "We present a triple contribution for structured IE test-time scaling: (1) a QE framework showing confidence signals reliably predict output quality and enable selective prediction (+5-8pp @80% coverage); (2) a diagnostic revealing that the correlation-selection gap is fundamental — persisting from 4B to 72B and from fine-tuned to zero-shot regimes — driven by degeneracy, LP compression, and LP-alignment misalignment; and (3) entity-level construction as a diagnostic-motivated mitigation that significantly improves over greedy decoding (+1.02pp SciERC, +1.40pp FewNERD fine-tuned; +1.53pp SciERC zero-shot via LP-weighting), with effectiveness governed by oracle headroom."

**Title candidates**:
- "Don't Select, Construct: Diagnosing and Fixing Test-Time Scaling for Structured Information Extraction"
- "Strong Predictors, Weak Selectors: From Diagnosis to Entity-Level Construction for Structured IE"
- "Beyond Selection: Entity-Level Construction as the Correct Self-Consistency for Structured IE"

## Anticipated Reviewer Concerns

### R1: "Only one NER dataset — generalization unclear"
- **Status**: ✅ RESOLVED. 3 NER datasets (SciERC + CoNLL-2003 + Few-NERD INTRA) × 2 models (Qwen3-8B + LLaMA-3.1-8B) + scale ablation (Qwen3-4B). Few-NERD adds 32,565 instances with distinct degeneracy profile (10% vs 21-58%). Cross-dataset comparison revealing LP alignment as primary selection predictor (D154) is the paper's strongest empirical contribution.
- **Priority**: P0, RESOLVED

### R2: "Only one model family (Qwen3-8B)"
- **Mitigation**: LLaMA-3.1-8B shows model-agnostic effect. ⚠️ **exp-007 数据被污染 (test data leakage)**，LLaMA SciERC 正确值来自 exp_018 (clean rerun)。unified_rho_full.json 的 LLaMA SciERC 条目必须替换为 exp_018 数据。正确 LLaMA SciERC N=8 3-seed mean: SJ 0.325, FK 0.256, VC 0.384, EM 0.279, LP 0.162。
- **Priority**: P0

### R3: "FK is a strawman baseline — what about log-prob, USC, exact-match?"
- **Mitigation**: exp-012 (log-prob), exp-013 (exact-match), exp-014 (entity voting) provide comprehensive baseline comparison. Results: structural consistency family (EM+SJ+voting) >> log-prob >> FK. USC discussed in related work (LLM-as-judge, orthogonal approach).
- **Priority**: P0, RESOLVED — results decisive

### R3b: "EM beats voting_conf and SJ on AUROC — why present SJ/voting_conf?"
- **Mitigation**: EM is a strict binary signal (all-or-nothing match); SJ captures partial agreement and generalizes to arbitrary structured outputs (relations, events). Voting_conf provides granular entity-level scores. NER full AUROC: EM 0.749 > SJ 0.692 > voting_conf 0.684, but ρ: voting_conf 0.379 > SJ 0.360 > EM 0.295. EM excels at binary discrimination but underperforms on rank ordering. SJ is also more temperature-robust (Δρ=±0.01). Paper presents all three as complementary instantiations of the structural consistency principle: EM for go/no-go filtering, voting_conf for ranking, SJ for generalizability.
- **Priority**: P1 — narrative adjusted for 1024-token results

### R4: "No actual TTS improvement demonstrated"
- **Status**: ✅ CONFIRMED by exp_016_rerun_1024_bootstrap. No signal significantly outperforms greedy on either task. NER logprob +0.6pp not significant (bootstrap p=0.39, 95% CI [−0.030, +0.042], Cohen's d=0.038). RE: greedy > all signals.
- **Mitigation**: Paper PIVOTS to "confidence estimation + correlation-selection gap analysis." exp-006 redesigned as diagnostic: show selection curves to visualize the gap (F1 vs N per signal + oracle ceiling). The gap itself is a contribution, not a failure.
- **Priority**: P0 — narrative pivot complete, bootstrap confirms

### R5: "Sample size N=8 may be too small for reliable SJ estimation"
- **Mitigation**: exp-001 (N=16) with multi-seed robustness
- **Priority**: P0

### R6: "Conditional analysis cherry-picks favorable instances"
- **Mitigation**: Principled separation (knowledge-gap vs uncertainty). Add threshold sensitivity analysis. Temperature analysis provides independent validation.
- **Priority**: P0 (add sensitivity analysis)

### R7: "Only ρ as evaluation metric"
- **Mitigation**: Add AUROC, calibration plots (ECE), Kendall's τ for all experiments. ECE data now available: NER best calibrated = EM (0.353), RE best = voting (0.272). Logprob worst calibrated (NER 0.706, RE 0.769).

  - Semantic uncertainty (Kuhn 2023), calibration (Kadavath 2022, Guo 2017, Desai & Durrett 2020)

  - **[2025-2026 新颖性自查补充 — 必引]**:
    - CISC (ACL Findings 2025) — confidence-weighted majority vote for reasoning; 对比：我们用 structural similarity 而非 confidence 加权，且面向 set-structured IE 输出
    - Self-Certainty Best-of-N (ICLR 2026, arxiv 2502.18581) — KL-divergence reward-free selection; 对比：我们发现 log-prob 是唯一有效 selection signal (与其方向互补)，且揭示 correlation-selection gap

# 论文写作风格规范

> 核心哲学：**论文是一个有说服力的故事，不是实验报告。** 审稿人在几十秒内判断论文价值——如果 Abstract 和 Introduction 读起来像实验日志，论文就已经失败了。

---

## 一、总体写作哲学

### 1.1 故事驱动，不是数据堆砌

- 论文必须以"故事线"为核心展开：问题 → 洞察 → 方法 → 验证
- 禁止大量实验数据堆砌——每个数字出现必须服务于叙事推进
- 附录内容必须在正文中有明确引用且融入叙事，禁止简单堆砌
- 如果附录数据对核心叙事有重大影响，根据附录数据调整论文 framing

### 1.2 主线统一性

- 当 idea 在研究过程中发生变化后，**必须重审全文逻辑**
- 常见问题：Introduction 讲的故事 A，Method 做的是故事 B，Results 又在讲故事 C
- 修复方式：从最终实验结论反推，重写 Introduction 的问题定义和动机
- 每次 idea 调整后检查：Abstract → Introduction → Method → Results → Discussion → Conclusion 是否形成一条连贯主线

### 1.3 专有名词必须有定义

- 首次出现的专有名词/缩写必须给出完整定义和解释
- Abstract 中使用的缩写也必须在 Abstract 内定义（如 LLM = Large Language Model）
- 不能假设读者知道你自己定义的术语——论文从来没解释过的概念不能直接使用
- 通用规则：如果一个非标准术语第一次出现时没有括号定义，就是写作 bug

### 1.4 写作前必读同类优秀论文

- 每个章节动笔前，找 **2-3 篇目标会议近 1-2 年的高分论文**作为风格参考——同类问题或同类方法皆可
- 重点学：
  - Abstract 怎么用最少篇幅讲完故事
  - Introduction 怎么从大问题切入到具体贡献
  - Related Work 怎么 positioning 自己（不是 survey）
  - Table/Figure 怎么压缩信息密度
- **不是抄袭**，是学习同行的故事节奏和审美——不同子领域叙事节奏差异很大
- 实操：Paper Agent 可以从 `literature_map.yaml` 中挑 `role=foundation` 或 `role=direct-competitor` 的论文，把 `{title, venue, year, abstract}` 附在 Worker 的 task_prompt 中作为概念参考；如需学习写作风格本身，让 Worker 通过 WebSearch 取得论文链接并 fetch 全文

---

## 二、Abstract 写作规范

### 2.1 四个必答问题（150-250 words）

Abstract 必须在很短的篇幅内清楚回答：
1. **研究什么问题** — 1-2 句话交代背景和痛点
2. **为什么重要** — 现有方法的不足（不用写太多）
3. **本文提出什么** — 核心贡献的关键机制（简要，不堆砌细节）
4. **结果说明什么** — 用具体实验结论支撑贡献

### 2.2 禁忌

- **禁止堆砌数据**：Abstract 不是 Results 的缩写。最多引用 2-3 个关键数字，要服务于 claim
- **禁止过度宣传**：不说 "revolutionary"、"groundbreaking"
- **禁止写成 Introduction 的缩写**：Abstract 是独立阅读单元
- **禁止术语堆积**：如果审稿人几十秒内判断不出价值，就失败了
- **缩写必须定义**：Abstract 中首次出现的缩写必须展开

### 2.3 审稿人视角检验

写完后用这个标准自检：审稿人能否在 30 秒内判断——
- 问题是否重要？
- 方法是否清楚？
- 贡献是否可信？
- 结果是否有说服力？

---

## 三、Introduction 写作规范

### 3.1 完整叙事线（5 段结构）

Introduction 需要从一个清晰、重要的问题切入，逐步把读者带到核心贡献：

1. **研究背景**（1-2 段）：大模型在某类能力/应用中已取得进展，但仍存在一个关键瓶颈
2. **问题重要性**（1 段）：结合真实应用、已有方法局限或当前趋势，说明这不是小问题
3. **现有方法不足**（1 段）：系统梳理为什么不够（依赖更大模型/更多数据/更复杂推理/更高成本，或只在特定 benchmark 有效）
4. **本文核心想法**（1 段）：我们观察到什么、提出了什么方法、为什么能解决上述问题
5. **贡献总结**（列表）：清楚列出方法贡献、实验贡献和分析贡献

\section{Introduction}\label{sec:introduction}

Test-time compute scaling has emerged as a complement to model scaling \cite{snell2025scaling}: repeated sampling with majority voting \citep{wang2023selfconsistency}, best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, brown2024monkeys}, and extended chain-of-thought \cite{muennighoff2025s1} yield large gains on reasoning and code generation, but the evidence concentrates on tasks with discrete answers or execution-based verification.
Named entity recognition (NER) poses a structurally different challenge: the output is a \textit{set} of entities, two samples may extract overlapping but non-identical sets, and there is no obvious majority to vote on.
This challenge generalizes to any \textit{set-valued} structured prediction task where outputs admit partial but not exact overlap.

Prior work on confidence estimation for LLM-based IE has conflated \textit{quality estimation} (which inputs does the model handle reliably?) with \textit{sample selection} (which of $N$ outputs is best?).
Existing self-consistency methods \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, chen2024usc, taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty} assume outputs can be grouped by equivalence, an assumption that breaks for entity sets with partial overlap.
Unlike \citet{yao2026consistency}, who demonstrate that self-consistency correlates with task accuracy, we provide the first systematic empirical characterization of \textit{when and why} test-time scaling via LP-based selection succeeds or fails for structured prediction, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as the two blocking mechanisms.

A key distinction structures our analysis: four of five signals (Soft Jaccard, voting confidence, Fleiss' $\kappa$, exact match) are instance-level aggregates that assign identical scores to all $N$ candidates for a given input; only log-probability (LP) is natively per-sample.
All signals achieve reliable quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82; Figure~\ref{fig:overview}), supporting selective prediction.
For selection, LP achieves $+1.39$~pp on Few-NERD ($p{<}0.001$) in settings where both low instance degeneracy and adequate alignment are present, with gains scaling with $N$.
On SciERC, the observed LP gain ($+0.2$~pp, $p{=}0.29$) falls below the minimum detectable effect (${\approx}$1.5~pp at 80\% power, $n{=}529$) despite 13~pp oracle headroom. We term this disparity between quality estimation strength and selection effectiveness the \textbf{correlation-selection gap}.
Three factors qualitatively shape this gap: (a)~\textit{instance degeneracy} (13\textendash 68\% across our benchmarks) compresses the candidate space; (b)~\textit{oracle headroom} bounds the achievable gain; (c)~\textit{LP-quality alignment} (within-instance $\rho(\text{LP}, \text{F1})$) determines whether LP can discriminate candidates in non-degenerate instances (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}).
Our diagnosis complements MBR utility misalignment \cite{eikema2025structured}: degeneracy eliminates candidate diversity before utility alignment matters (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).
Both mechanisms intensify with model capability: degeneracy rises with training convergence and varies across model families rather than scaling monotonically with parameter count (\S\ref{sec:scaling}). This creates a tension between model quality and test-time improvability.

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{fig_overview}
\caption{Overview of the correlation-selection gap. \textbf{Left}: consistency signals estimate instance quality ($\rho$ up to 0.45; Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}). \textbf{Center}: instance-level signals assign identical scores to all $N$ candidates, so selection cannot outperform greedy. \textbf{Right}: entity-level construction via majority vote ($\theta{=}2/N$) bypasses the bottleneck ($+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD; \S\ref{sec:prescriptive}).}
\label{fig:overview}
\end{figure*}

We evaluate five signals on four NER benchmarks (SciERC \cite{luan2018scierc}, Few-NERD \cite{ding2021fewnerd}, CoNLL-2003 \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll}, WNUT-17 \cite{derczynski2017wnut}) spanning a difficulty gradient, using two 8B models (Qwen3-8B, LLaMA-3.1-8B) with a 4B ablation, varying $N{\in}\{2,\ldots,32\}$ and model capacity across 4B\textendash 8B fine-tuned and 72B zero-shot regimes.
Our contributions:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item \textbf{Quality estimation as a test-time scaling diagnostic.}
    Five signals from three families evaluated on four NER benchmarks, two model families, and a 4B ablation, achieving reliable quality estimation ($\rho$ up to 0.45, AUROC up to 0.82).
    QE enables selective prediction: filtering low-confidence instances at 80\% coverage yields $+5$--$8$\,pp F1 (AUPRC 0.70--0.92, VC strongest; \S\ref{sec:prescriptive}).

    \item \textbf{Failure modes of test-time scaling for structured prediction.}
    For fine-tuned 4B--8B models, LP-quality alignment (within-instance $\rho(\text{LP}, \text{F1})$) is the primary predictor of selection success: LP achieves $+1.39$~pp on Few-NERD ($p{<}0.001$) where alignment is strong, but not on benchmarks with weak alignment.
    Instance degeneracy causally modulates LP within fixed settings (epoch and temperature ablations) but does not predict cross-dataset direction ($\rho{=}0.052$, 23 configurations); supervised combinations and hidden state probes (Appendix~\ref{app:hidden_probe}) confirm the gap persists.
    The resulting three-step diagnostic (measure degeneracy, assess signal alignment, choose aggregation) provides a reusable protocol for structured test-time scaling (\S\ref{sec:discussion}).

    \item \textbf{Entity-level construction as a partial mitigation for structured test-time scaling failures.}
    The diagnostic naturally motivates entity-level aggregation, adapting entity voting from ensemble NER \cite{florian2003named} to stochastic sampling: under fine-tuning and zero-shot regimes, LP-weighted construction yields $+1.40$\,pp on Few-NERD and $+1.02$\,pp on SciERC (multi-seed mean, $p{<}0.005$; \S\ref{sec:prescriptive}).
    Construction and LP selection are complementary, governed by LP-quality alignment.
\end{enumerate}

1	\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}
2	
3	Effective selection likely requires content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, venktesh2025trust}.
4	Three factors constrain selection: degeneracy (17.8--67.9\%), limited headroom, and LP-quality alignment ($\rho$ 0.043--0.667); within non-degenerate instances, MBR utility correlates with F1 ($\rho{=}0.524$) \cite{eikema2022sampling}.
5	Where LP compression is mitigated (range ${\geq}0.05$, $n{=}210$), LP yields $+2.9$~pp ($p{=}0.004$; Table~\ref{tab:nontied_main}), though $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ is post-hoc ($p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.14$; Appendix~\ref{app:epsilon_robustness}).
6	Temperature disentangles degeneracy from alignment: at $T{=}1.2$, degeneracy drops to 14.9\% yet LP does not improve ($\rho{=}0.225$; Table~\ref{tab:t_degeneracy}); the selection window narrows with model improvement \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, snell2025scaling}.
7	
8	\paragraph{From diagnosis to practice.}\label{sec:selection_method}
9	Entity-level construction bypasses both failure mechanisms (Table~\ref{tab:entity_construction}). Degeneracy gates effectiveness: across seven conditions (two model families, two prompting regimes, three datasets), gains are positive when degeneracy ${<}22$\% and absent when ${>}31$\% (all $p{<}0.01$; epoch ablations confirm within-dataset, Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}). Under 72B few-shot, construction fails despite low degeneracy, indicating that demonstrations alter diversity structure beyond simple error correlation (Appendix~\ref{app:fs_error}). QE signals remain effective under few-shot (SJ $\rho$ 0.29--0.44), confirming that quality estimation is regime-independent even when construction is not.

Effective selection likely requires content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, venktesh2025trust}.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey}, and calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.

\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).
Fine-tuning \cite{kirk2024understanding} and constrained decoding \cite{holtzman2020curious, vijayakumar2018diverse} both limit the diversity recoverable for selection.

\section{Related Work}\label{sec:related}

\paragraph{Test-time compute scaling.}
Test-time compute scaling encompasses three families: (a) extended chain-of-thought reasoning \cite{muennighoff2025s1}, (b) repeated sampling with majority voting (self-consistency; \citealp{wang2023selfconsistency}) and its extensions to free-form text \cite{chen2024usc, thirukovalluru2024atomic, manakul2023selfcheckgpt}, and (c) best-of-$N$ selection via compute-optimal allocation \cite{snell2025scaling, brown2024monkeys}.
Reward-free selectors \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc, kang2025selfcertainty, wang2025rankedvoting, oh2026latentsc} and adaptive gating variants \cite{aggarwal2023adaptive, wang2025make, feng2025optimal, kim2026reasc} reduce inference cost; \citet{chen2025twofailures} diagnose failure modes.
All target discrete-answer reasoning; structured prediction requires different aggregation mechanisms because degeneracy operates at the entity-set level.

\paragraph{Consistency for structured IE.}
\citet{yao2026consistency} show consistency correlates with accuracy for LLM-based NER/RE; we show correlation alone does not ensure selection gains, diagnosing degeneracy and compression as blocking mechanisms.
CoCoA \cite{vashurin2025cocoa} fuses confidence with consistency; our supervised baseline confirms combination is not the bottleneck (\S\ref{sec:robustness_main}).
Earlier work on confidence for structured prediction \cite{culotta2004confidence, mejer2010confidence, fomicheva2020unsupervised} establishes the paradigm we extend to set-valued outputs.
Ensemble approaches aggregate predictions from multiple models or prompts \cite{florian2003named, xiao2025el4ner}; \citet{xie2023zeroshot} propose two-stage entity voting for zero-shot NER, the closest prior work to our entity-level construction.
LLM-Blender \cite{jiang2023llmblender} fuses outputs from multiple LLMs via pairwise ranking, whereas our single-model stochastic sampling derives diversity from temperature rather than model heterogeneity.
Our entity-level construction aggregates across samples from a single fine-tuned model, without requiring model diversity or prompt engineering.
Our evaluation builds on generative IE \cite{zhou2024uniner, sainz2024gollie, li2023codeie, wadhwa2023revisiting, xie2024selfimproving} and constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided, dong2024xgrammar, park2024grammar, schall2025hidden}.
\citet{yun2025price} show structured formats induce diversity collapse; our LP compression (median range 0.041 nats; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) corroborates this for NER.

\paragraph{Uncertainty estimation and MBR decoding.}
Surveys cover confidence estimation \cite{geng2024confidence}, uncertainty quantification \cite{xia2025survey}, and calibration \cite{hobelsberger2025systematic}; semantic uncertainty \cite{kuhn2023semantic, farquhar2024detecting} and P(True) \cite{kadavath2022language} provide model-internal alternatives.
Our selection strategies instantiate MBR decoding \cite{eikema2022sampling, deguchi2024centroid}; unlike MT where MBR yields consistent gains \cite{freitag2022high} and code generation where execution-based MBR improves selection \cite{shi2022mbr}, instance degeneracy eliminates the headroom MBR needs even when utility is well-aligned ($\rho{=}0.52$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}).
\citet{eikema2025structured} find MBR utilities degrade on structured outputs; our diagnosis is complementary: degeneracy, not utility misalignment, is the primary bottleneck.
Our QE results connect to selective prediction \cite{geifman2017selective, kuleshov2015calibrated, varshney2022investigating}: signals with AUROC up to 0.82 support abstention policies independent of sample selection.

\paragraph{Best-of-$N$ with learned verifiers.}
\citet{gao2023scaling} establish BoN scaling laws and \citet{chen2021evaluating} define the pass@$k$ metric for code generation; our unsupervised signals face a more fundamental limitation than reward overoptimization.
Trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, lightman2024verify, fernandes2022quality} and self-evaluation guided search \cite{xie2023selfevaluation} learn per-sample scoring.
CISC \cite{taubenfeld2025cisc} and Self-Certainty \cite{kang2025selfcertainty} derive per-sample confidence from hidden states rather than output statistics, but require architecture-specific access to intermediate representations; these hidden-state signals remain untested for structured prediction (\S Limitations).
Fine-tuning \cite{kirk2024understanding} and constrained decoding \cite{holtzman2020curious, vijayakumar2018diverse} both limit the diversity recoverable for selection.

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

Effective selection likely requires content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, venktesh2025trust}.
Three factors constrain selection: degeneracy (17.8--67.9\%), limited headroom, and LP-quality alignment ($\rho$ 0.043--0.667); within non-degenerate instances, MBR utility correlates with F1 ($\rho{=}0.524$) \cite{eikema2022sampling}.
Where LP compression is mitigated (range ${\geq}0.05$, $n{=}210$), LP yields $+2.9$~pp ($p{=}0.004$; Table~\ref{tab:nontied_main}), though $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ is post-hoc ($p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.14$; Appendix~\ref{app:epsilon_robustness}).
Temperature disentangles degeneracy from alignment: at $T{=}1.2$, degeneracy drops to 14.9\% yet LP does not improve ($\rho{=}0.225$; Table~\ref{tab:t_degeneracy}); the selection window narrows with model improvement \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, snell2025scaling}.

\paragraph{From diagnosis to practice.}\label{sec:selection_method}
Entity-level construction bypasses both failure mechanisms (Table~\ref{tab:entity_construction}). Degeneracy gates effectiveness: across seven conditions (two model families, two prompting regimes, three datasets), gains are positive when degeneracy ${<}22$\% and absent when ${>}31$\% (all $p{<}0.01$; epoch ablations confirm within-dataset, Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}). Under 72B few-shot, construction fails despite low degeneracy, indicating that demonstrations alter diversity structure beyond simple error correlation (Appendix~\ref{app:fs_error}). QE signals remain effective under few-shot (SJ $\rho$ 0.29--0.44), confirming that quality estimation is regime-independent even when construction is not.
Alternative strategies (DALS, MBR, DGS) fail to beat greedy (Appendix~\ref{app:dals}); supervised signal mixtures (logistic regression on all five signals) do not outperform the best single signal (Appendix~\ref{app:supervised_combination}).
These negative results are specific to fine-tuned models with constrained decoding (Appendix~\ref{app:when_selection_works}).
NER calibration is reasonable (ECE 0.069--0.096; Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}); conformal prediction could provide distribution-free coverage guarantees on top of our QE signals, though integrating conformal methods with set-valued structured outputs remains open.

\section{Discussion}\label{sec:discussion}

Effective selection likely requires content-aware verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers, venktesh2025trust}.
Three factors constrain selection: degeneracy (17.8--67.9\%), limited headroom, and LP-quality alignment ($\rho$ 0.043--0.667); within non-degenerate instances, MBR utility correlates with F1 ($\rho{=}0.524$) \cite{eikema2022sampling}.
Where LP compression is mitigated (range ${\geq}0.05$, $n{=}210$), LP yields $+2.9$~pp ($p{=}0.004$; Table~\ref{tab:nontied_main}), though $\varepsilon{=}0.05$ is post-hoc ($p_{\text{adj}}{=}0.14$; Appendix~\ref{app:epsilon_robustness}).
Temperature disentangles degeneracy from alignment: at $T{=}1.2$, degeneracy drops to 14.9\% yet LP does not improve ($\rho{=}0.225$; Table~\ref{tab:t_degeneracy}); the selection window narrows with model improvement \cite{wang2023selfconsistency, snell2025scaling}.

\paragraph{From diagnosis to practice.}\label{sec:selection_method}
Entity-level construction bypasses both failure mechanisms (Table~\ref{tab:entity_construction}). Degeneracy gates effectiveness: across seven conditions (two model families, two prompting regimes, three datasets), gains are positive when degeneracy ${<}22$\% and absent when ${>}31$\% (all $p{<}0.01$; epoch ablations confirm within-dataset, Appendix~\ref{app:epoch_confound}). Under 72B few-shot, construction fails despite low degeneracy, indicating that demonstrations alter diversity structure beyond simple error correlation (Appendix~\ref{app:fs_error}). QE signals remain effective under few-shot (SJ $\rho$ 0.29--0.44), confirming that quality estimation is regime-independent even when construction is not.
Alternative strategies (DALS, MBR, DGS) fail to beat greedy (Appendix~\ref{app:dals}); supervised signal mixtures (logistic regression on all five signals) do not outperform the best single signal (Appendix~\ref{app:supervised_combination}).
These negative results are specific to fine-tuned models with constrained decoding (Appendix~\ref{app:when_selection_works}).
NER calibration is reasonable (ECE 0.069--0.096; Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}); conformal prediction could provide distribution-free coverage guarantees on top of our QE signals, though integrating conformal methods with set-valued structured outputs remains open.
